title: Strata Shadow Allocator and Idle Migration playbook for KV fragmentation reduction
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Continuous batching workloads create heterogeneous KV entry sizes and lifetimes. Over time this leads to interleaved small and large KV regions, internal fragmentation, and wasted GPU memory that reduces effective model capacity and forces more frequent costly fallbacks. Existing compaction/defrag approaches (epochal rewrites, eager slab coalescing) either cause high tail latency when triggered or require large pauses.

Proposal: Implement a Strata Shadow Allocator (SSA) plus Idle Migration playbook. SSA organizes the KV arena into lightweight strata driven by per-worker sequence-length histograms and recent access signatures. Instead of moving live active entries synchronously, we maintain a shadow indirection map that lets the allocator point hot lookups to a compacted target region while the real relocation happens opportunistically during idle GPU cycles. Parallel components: a residence score computed from access recency and batch-size correlation, a drift-correcting reshuffle policy (gamma threshold) that triggers micro-swaps only when projected free-byte gain exceeds relocation cost, and a relocation ledger for safe rollback and telemetry.

Why different: This design minimizes synchronous rewrite work by separating logical compaction (indirection updates) from physical memory movement, enabling small incremental background coalesces that exploit GPU low-utilization windows and avoid disrupting latency SLOs. It also introduces a short-lived shadow tier that absorbs churn from mixed-length requests and provides a graceful path for rollback if a relocation increases cache miss rate.

High-level goals: reduce measured "wasted_kv_bytes" by at least 40% under mixed-length RLHF-like workloads, keep 95th-percentile generation latency regression <= 2% during background migration, and enable safe live rollouts with telemetry-driven auto-tuning of gamma thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Wasted_kv_bytes metric shows >=40% reduction on benchmark mixed-length workload compared to baseline (runtime-1.18) within two weeks of feature on production canary.
p95 generation latency degradation due to background migration <= 2% across canary traffic slices during a 72-hour observation window.
No data-corruption incidents in relocation ledger during at-scale canary (automated property checks and checksum validation pass).
Opportunistic idle migrations must not increase GPU memory high-water mark by >3% during migration windows.
Console telemetry exposes per-stratum fragmentation heatmaps, relocation cost histograms, and a tuning knob for gamma threshold; docs updated and runbook published.
implementation_plan: Design: formalize stratum keying scheme (recent sequence-length histogram + model signature) and indirection table layout (compact GPU-resident map).
Runtime: implement SSA allocator in C++ runtime with GPU-friendly contiguous movers and a relocation ledger (append-only, checksumed).
Scheduler integration: extend batching scheduler to emit short TTL hints for expected sequence-length distribution for the next 30s window.
Telemetry: add fragmentation heatmap and relocation cost metrics to Console; wire alerts for 'relocation_spike' and 'failed_rollback'.
Safety: implement canary flags to perform indirection-only compaction first (logical compaction without physical copy), then enable background micro-swaps gradually.
Performance testing: microbench in CI + GPU perf lab under varying batch shape mixes (10/50/200 token tails).
PRs: split into allocator core, scheduler hints, telemetry + console, and canary rollout orchestration.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (lab): run SSA allocator against synthetic workloads in GPU perf lab; iterate on gamma thresholds and micro-swap size.
Stage 1 (internal canary): enable indirection-only mode for 5% of internal traffic; monitor fragmentation and correctness for 7 days.
Stage 2 (background micro-swaps): enable opportunistic physical moves during low-util windows for 1% external canary; monitor p95 and relocation cost.
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): increase to 10% then 50% traffic while enabling auto-tuning; keep rollback path tested and ready.
Stage 4 (global): flip default, expose gamma tuning in Console, and run a 72-hour verification for SLA metrics.
risks: Indirection blowup: too many shadow entries increase pointer-chasing overhead and harm lookup latency. Mitigation: cap shadow residency by LRU & promote/demote heuristics.
Relocation thrash: incorrect gamma tuning can cause repeated moves. Mitigation: add exponential backoff per-token-group and telemetry alerts to freeze migrations if thrash detected.
GPU contention: large micro-swaps at wrong times spike utilization. Mitigation: use conservative migration budget per-GPU and integrate with scheduler to reserve low-util slices.
Rollback correctness: incomplete ledger entries could leave stale pointers. Mitigation: checksumed ledger, atomic switch steps, and preflight validation applied in canary phases.
test_plan: Unit tests for indirection map correctness, relocation ledger append/read, and checksum validation.
Integration tests: simulate mixed-length traffic with a model harness and assert fragmentation improvement without latency regressions.
Chaos tests: kill relocation workers mid-copy to ensure rollback path preserves logical mapping and no memory leaks occur.
Perf lab: run 48-hour soak with RLHF-like tails and measure wasted_kv_bytes, throughput, and p95 latency.
Canary verification checklist for each rollout stage (metrics thresholds and automated rollback triggers).
